title: Idempotency and retries
objective: Make "try again" safe: retry when replies get lost, without charging anyone twice.

sources.title: Stripe: Designing robust and predictable APIs with idempotency

simplifies: The server always succeeds; only replies get lost (20% here, illustrative), and the client retries after 400 ms up to 4 times, with no delay growing between tries. Real clients add exponential backoff with jitter, and servers keep idempotency keys only for a limited time.

challenges.title: Don't give up
challenges.prompt: 20% of replies are lost on the way back. Keep the payments users see failing at 1% or less for 10 seconds.

predict.prompt: The payment went through, but its reply was lost. What does the app see?

options.text: A timeout: it can't tell whether the payment happened
options.explanation: Right. A lost reply looks exactly like a failure from the outside.
The success message is the reply that was lost.
Nothing says it failed; the app just hears nothing.

challenges.hint: When the app hears nothing, what could it do instead of giving up?
challenges.explain: Retrying on timeout fixes what users see. But look at "Double charges": some of those payments had already gone through, and the retry charged them again.

challenges.title: Never charge twice
challenges.prompt: Retries are on. Keep double charges at zero the whole time for 10 seconds.

predict.prompt: A retry reaches the server for a payment it already processed. Without an idempotency key, what happens?

options.explanation: Right. The server can't tell a retry from a brand-new payment.
It has no way to know it is a repeat.

challenges.hint: What if every try of the same payment carried the same unique key?
challenges.explain: With an idempotency key, the server remembers keys it has processed and returns the first result for a repeat instead of charging again. Retries become safe.

options.text: Doing it twice has the same effect as doing it once
options.explanation: Right. Then a retry can't cause harm.
It can fail; what matters is that repeating it is safe.

options.text: Set my email address to x@example.com
options.explanation: Right. Setting it twice leaves the same result.
Each try sends another message unless it carries a key.
